findings.title: Login-cache invalidation decision uses the organization-aware wrapper, so updates can leave stale entries
findings.body: `update()` obtains `idpById` from `getById()`, which returns the anonymous `IdentityProviderModel` subclass created by `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel()`. That wrapper's `isEnabled()` returns false whenever the owning organization (or organizations support for the realm) is disabled, regardless of the IDP's own `enabled` flag. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate()` then evaluates `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` on this wrapper, so for any org-linked IDP whose organization is currently disabled the predicate is false. If the update also leaves the *new* model ineligible (e.g. only `hideOnLogin` is flipped to true, or `linkOnly` toggled) the method early-returns and no login cache key is invalidated, even though the cached id list (built from a DB query that only filters on the IDP's own attributes) does contain / should now contain that id. After the organization is re-enabled the login lists are served from the stale cache: a `hideOnLogin=true` provider keeps being rendered on the login page, or a newly un-hidden provider stays missing. The comparison should be done against the raw delegate model (e.g. `idpDelegate.getById(...)`) rather than the org-aware wrapper.

findings.title: Login query cache keyed only by realm+mode grows with the number of organizations and is rebuilt per new org
findings.body: `getForLogin` stores all results for a realm/fetch-mode in a single `IdentityProviderListQuery` whose internal map is keyed by `organizationId`. For `FetchMode.ALL` each per-organization entry contains the full set of realm-level login IDP ids plus that org's ids, so memory is O(#organizations * #realm login IDPs) per realm. Worse, every time a not-yet-cached organization id is seen the code calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and re-adds a merged query (lines 236-240), i.e. the whole entry for the realm is discarded and rebuilt on the hot login path. In realms with many organizations this means repeated full rebuilds instead of a stable cache. Note also that for `REALM_ONLY` the `organizationId` argument is ignored by the implementation, yet it is still used as the search key, producing redundant duplicate entries for every organization.

findings.title: Cleanup registered for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created providers
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` (lines 381 and 425) registers 21 cleanup tasks against a provider whose alias is the literal string `"alias"`, which never exists. The 21 providers actually created (`idp-alias-0` ... `idp-alias-20`) are therefore never removed, and the cleanup call itself will hit a 404. Depending on whether the realm is re-imported per method this either fails the cleanup phase or leaks providers into other test methods — e.g. `testCacheIDPByOrg` asserts exact counts (6 IDPs for orga) and `testCacheIDPForLogin` asserts 5/5/10, so leftovers make the suite order-dependent and flaky. Use the real alias variable (the same bug exists at line 303 and should be fixed there too).

findings.title: No coverage for login-cache invalidation on create/remove of a login-eligible provider
findings.body: The new test only exercises `create()` and `remove()` with providers that are *not* eligible for login (`hideOnLogin=true` provider created, disabled `idp-alias-1` removed) and asserts the caches survive. The two new `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...)` call sites in `create()` and `remove()` for an eligible provider are never verified, so a regression where creating or deleting a login-visible IDP fails to invalidate the per-realm login caches (leaving the login page showing a deleted broker, or hiding a new one) would not be caught.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate no longer matches LoginFilter/getLoginSearchOptions contract
findings.body: `LoginFilter` is documented as the enum that "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", and `getLoginSearchOptions()` is used to build the equivalent DB query. The predicate now additionally requires `organizationId == null || config[kc.org.broker.public] == true`, a condition that is not represented in the enum nor in `getLoginSearchOptions()`. Callers that rely on the two being equivalent filters (query vs. in-memory predicate) will now get different result sets for org-linked providers; the javadoc/enum should be updated or the organization condition expressed as part of the filter set so both paths stay in sync.
